newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close lower on late profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close lower on late profit-taking.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Tuesday following late profit-taking that thwarted the index's bid to stand above the 10,000-point psychological barrier, brokers said.
The benchmark stock index surged to an intra-day peak of 10,057.95 in early trade, but lost steam in late session to finish at 9,892.34, down 30.71 points or 0.31 percent from Monday's close.
Turnover was heavy at T$224.39 billion.
Brokers said investors became cautious after the index surged past the 10,000 level.
They said selling of high-priced electronics shares was persistent since opening with microchip giant Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co losing continually to close T$10 lower at T$146.
United Microelectronics, whose performance often reflects that of strong rival Taiwan Semiconductor, lost T$5.5 at T$134. Acer Sertek, an arm of computer giant Acer Inc, dipped T$7 to T$104.
Acer Inc edged down T$0.5 to T$98, back from its early gains.

"The announcement by Dutch Philips Electronic NV to sell 100 million shares of Taiwan Semiconductor in the local bourse was the major reason of the heavy loss of the chip giant," said Lin long-hsien of United Securities.
Brokers said high-prices shares like those of United Microelectronics and Acer Inc had risen sharply for some time.
"It was healthy for the prices of these shares to go down," National Securities' Alex Yang said.
Other sectors, including financials, textiles, papers, cements and plastics, all posted gains, with papers and cements being the gain leaders, rising 3.24 and 2.46 percent, respectively.
Brokers said there was chance in the next few days for the index to stand firm above the 10,000-point level.
"The electronics fever has cooled down, while other major sectors have seen moderate growth today. This means the market is back on a healthy track," National Securities' Oliver Fang said.
Electronics, which had risen sharply, had been the sector to carry the market in recent days.
A 9,900-10,200 range was seen for Wednesday.
